memory.note: Verified 2026-09-05 on this machine: `kimi --help` lists `--add-dir <dir>` (repeatable), `-m/--model`, `--auto` (Never Ask mode) and `-y/--yolo`, and describes `-c` as continuing 'the previous session for the working directory'. ~/.kimi-code/sessions holds wd_<basename>_<hash> directories and ~/.kimi-code/session_index.jsonl records a workDir per session, so the key is the cwd.

attention_patterns.message: Kimi has hit its rolling usage limit for this account. Nothing is broken and there is nothing to fix — wait for the window to roll over, or move this agent to another provider with `failover`.
attention_patterns.note: Anchored on the FRAGMENT, never on the whole observed string, and the first reason is empirical rather than theoretical. Measured across four live quota-blocked kimi panes on 2026-09-09 (%113, %24, %40, %14 — see docs/evidence/TM-131-quota-blocked-live-panes.md), the error renders TWO different ways: three panes show `Error: [provider.auth_error] 403 You've reached your 5-hour usage limit.` and %113 shows `Error: 403 You've reached your 5-hour usage limit.` inside a box-drawing frame, with no `[provider.auth_error]` prefix at all. A pattern anchored on the full string would have matched three panes and missed the fourth. The second reason is the tmux format parser: `[provider.auth_error]`'s colon would get the whole entry dropped by tmuxFailureTrigger, and a dropped pattern never fires on the subscription path at all, silently. Third, the fragment survives withoutPaths, which blanks whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/` — `5-hour` has none. `\d+` rather than a literal 5 because the window length is an account/plan property.

notes: --auto is Never Ask mode; -y/--yolo is the milder Ask When Needed. auto_approve uses --auto because the launcher cannot answer a prompt.
